deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment1_Specifications_1232SA26Q1239.pdf ===== SPECIFICATIONS 1.0 Speciﬁcations Description: Custom 4K Wheat SNP Targeted Amplicon Primer Pool Quantity: 1 Unit Type: Primer Pool (15,000 rxn) Minimum Requirements: The required item is the existing Euroﬁns-developed custom ~4,000-marker wheat SNP targeted amplicon primer pool. The primer pool must be the same custom primer pool previously developed by Euroﬁns BioDiagnostics and used in a small test run. The current procurement is for the same primer pool in a larger quantity. Minimum requirements: • Custom SNP primer pool must target approximately 4,000 SNPs within the wheat genome as determined by th

bread wheat, which has A, B, and D sub- genomes with extensive homoeologous and paralogous sequence similarity. • The supplied primer pool must be consistent with the Euroﬁns-developed design used for the small test run to maintain data continuity and avoid redesign/revalidation. 2.0 Place of Delivery USDA-ARS 410 SE Dairy Rd. Clark Hall 287 Pullman, WA 99164 Attn: Travis RuƯ 3.0 Delivery Schedule Item QTY Unit Place of Delivery Delivery Date 4K GBS Panel Development/Creation 1 Primer Pool (15,000 rxn) 410 SE. Dairy Rd., Clark Hall 287, Pullman, WA 99164 60 days after award 4.0 Additional Requirements Award is contingent upon satisfactory technical review and acceptance of the pending small-scale test- plate data generated using the same Euroﬁns-developed custom 4K wheat SNP targeted amplicon primer pool. If the test-plate data do not demonstrate acceptable performance for the intended wheat SNP genotyping application, including suƯicient sequence coverage/read depth per marker and per sample and usable genotype call quality, the Government may elect not to proceed with award or may revise/cancel the requirement prior to award. ===== FILE: files/C04_Solicitation_Terms_and_Conditions_1232SA26Q1239.pdf ===== 4K Wheat SNP Targeted Am

Because participation is voluntary, facilities may opt out or lack to comply with the testing schedule. The Contractor shall contact any facility that misses a collection date. If a facility misses an entire week of sample collection, the Contractor shall notify the CDC Project Manager in writing, including details of interactions with the facility and resolution status. If the Contractor cannot reach the facility after three attempts, CDC shall be notified. Facilities that consistently miss sampling events, defined as two or more missed collections within four weeks, shall also be reported to CDC. CDC may choose to replace non-responsive facilities. The Contractor shall document all communications and attempts. 5.6 The Contractor shall ensure all submitted data are accurate, complete, and comply with the designated data dictionary, including proper file types, formats, column headings, and data standards. General: 1.1 J. Clark National Wildlife Refuge is requesting a contractor to map noxious weeds (Leafy Spurge) and chemically spray those areas on refuge lands. Exact treatment areas will be provided to the contractor. The contractor will apply herbicides as specified in the approved Pesticide Use Proposals (PUPs) and product labels, including product selection, rates, adjuvants, and timing. Use adjuvants only as permitted by the label; specify type/rate per label & PUP. Maps showing the general area are included. All pesticide applications will comply with the law, FWS policies, and

complete the mapping and herbicide application (see maps, 140FS226Q0168 Chemical Application for Noxious Weed Control Page 2 of 3 J Clark Salyer National Wildlife Refuge 2 legal descriptions and estimated acres to be chemically treated). All herbicides approved for use will be provided by FWS. All equipment used in performance of this work shall be thoroughly cleaned and free of all debris, including soil, plant material, invasive species, and noxious weeds, prior to arrival on site. Equipment that does not meet this requirement will not be allowed to operate on site. The herbicide application and contractor must meet the following specifications: A. The contractor will use Method 240SL or Plateau herbicide with water as listed on the label to control invasive leafy spurge. B. All treatments will be made in accordance with manufactures instructions for use. C. Contractor will use only label‑approved adjuvants/drift agents at label‑specified rates. No unlisted adjuvants. Drift control agents and adjuvants must be approved for use with all herbicides and used in accordance with the herbicide label. D. Set swath width per manufacturer & calibration, verified by flow‑rate and pattern tests documented before full‑rate operations. E. Establish temporary closures and signage a

ith Worker Protection Standards (training, PPE, posting, REI). Follow labels, PUPs, and federal/state law. G. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. 1.2 Background: The National Mall and Memorial Parks where the nation comes to remember and where history is made. As “America’s Front Yard,” the National Mall and Memorial Parks is home to many of our country’s most iconic memorials telling the story of people and events that shaped us as a nation. Each year, millions of people come to recreate, commemorate presidential legacies, honor our veterans, and make their voices heard. For more than 200 years, the National Mall symbolized our nation and its democratic values, which have inspired the world. The National Mall - the great swath of green in the middle of our capital city and stretching from the foot of the United States Capitol to the Potomac River - is the premiere civic and symbolic space in our nation. 1.3 Objectives: The National Park Service, National Capital Region, National Mall and Memorial Parks is seeking contract services for preventative maintenance, and urgent and non-urgent repair services for the security doors and their cont

: All work is to be scheduled and coordinated through the Contracting Officers Representative. No entity owns or exercises control of the highest-level owner. Immediate owner means an entity, other than the offeror, that has direct control of the offeror. There may be more than one immediate owner (e.g., joint ventures). certifications_partner.text: najmniej 4 sloty na certyfikaty X.509 (PIV: Authentication, Signature, Key Management, Card Authentication) Obsługa algorytmów kryptograficznych RSA 2048 i/lub ECC P-256 (minimum), preferowane RSA 4096, ECC P-384 Kompatybilność z Windows AD Logowanie do domeny Windows bez dodatkowych sterowników (Smart Card Minidriver lub standard PC/SC) Stan urządzeń Fabrycznie nowe, nieużywane, oryginalne Gwarancja Minimum 2 lata 2. Kontekst techniczny i cel zamówienia Zamawiający eksploatuje infrastrukturę domenową opartą na Microsoft Active Directory z własnym Urzędem Certyfikacji (CA) działającym w oparciu o Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS). Dostarczone klucze bezpieczeństwa muszą umożliwiać: • Zapis certyfikatu użytkownika X.509 wydanego przez CA Zamawiającego do slotu PIV klucza (slot 9a – Authentication). • Logowanie do domeny Windows (Smart Card Logon) z wykorzystaniem certyfikatu przechowywanego w kluczu – bez konieczności wpisywania hasła domenowego. • Uwierzytelnianie przez NFC na urządzeniach mobilnych i czytnikach NFC. Strona 3 z 8 • Uwierzytelnianie FIDO2/U2F do aplikacji webowych i systemów obsługujących te standardy. • Opcjonalne: podpisywanie dokumentów i szyfrowanie poczty elektronicznej z użyciem certyfikatów PKI (sloty 9c i 9d). Kluc

The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification/socioeconomic status (service-disabled veteran owned small business, veteran owned small business, women owned small business, HUB Zone, 8(a), small business or large business), relative to NAICS 713990 with a size standard of $9 Million. Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. STATEMENT OF WORK 1.0 Introduction/Background North Texas VA Police officers are required to qualify on their assigned weapons on a quarterly basis. Overtime discharge of spent ammunition leads to accumulation of lead and other hazardous materials on range surfaces. Regular maintenance of the mobile firing range is essential to ensure safety and longevity of the equipment. Routine cleaning reduces exposure to hazardous materials such as lead dust, mitigates fire hazards, and ensures compliance with VA safety regulations. Failure to conduct regular maintenance could result in increased health risks, costly repairs, and possible suspension of range operations.

Failure to conduct regular maintenance could result in increased health risks, costly repairs, and possible suspension of range operations. 2.0 Objective Contractor shall deliver all supplies listed in Table 1 to North Texas Veterans Health Care System in accordance with the original manufacturer specifications. Bullet Trap and Range Cleaning Contractor shall perform bullet trap cleaning service up to two (2) times per year. Cleaning services shall include Removal and disposal of accumulated lead and debris from the bullet trap system. Replenishment of Ballistic Rubber Media. Utilization of Lead Abatement wipes and cleaners to clean all interior surfaces of the range. Contractor shall coordinate scheduling of cleaning visits with Anthony Camell and Maleisha Anderson a minimum of two (2) weeks in advance. Range Inspections Contractor shall conduct a comprehensive inspection of the range and container system two (2) times per year. Inspections

Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible.
